After our conversation, this is what I heard

Sheena, I wanted to put everything we discussed in one place so you could see the possibilities for Turtle Threads Collection.

I've developed several creative directions based on what you shared with me. Take your time looking through them. Together, we can decide which direction best represents your vision for the brand.

Here is what you told me, in your own words, so you can check that I got it right.

  • “I like things like this. A cartoon kind of look.” You like the drawn look. Bold lines. Bright and clear, like a picture that pops.
  • “Not too young. Still grown, but drawn.” Fun, but for grown women. Not childish. The drawing style, with a grown feel.
  • “It does not have to be a turtle.” The turtle can be in the logo, or it can stay out. What matters most is the feel.
  • “I had people pick one.” You showed the looks to people and let them choose the one they liked best. Their pick counts.

You said you didn't want that one, but you wanted something like this, so here it is, and there are more ways to go.

The logo, on the pieces

A logo has to live somewhere. Here it is where it will live: on a sweatshirt, a cap, a sewn-in label, a hoodie, and a tote bag.

The feel of the brand

This one is not a logo. It is the feel the clothes walk in with. Braids with gold in them. Green shades. Green and gold worn bold and proud. The logo has to match this energy.

Thank you, Sheena.

The photo shoot

One day of shooting for Turtle Threads Collection, built around the clothes and the women who wear them.

  • The dateSaturday, December 12, 2026, in Maryland. We choose the studio together.
  • The modelsThree women, in different sizes, so the clothes are seen the way real customers wear them.
  • The looksSeven to eight looks in the day, with jackets and pajamas in the mix.
  • The dayAbout four hours of shooting, plus time to set up and pack up, in a full studio.
  • The shotsEach woman on her own. All three together. Close shots of the clothes. And shots that feel like real life.
  • The workPhotography and video. Every look gets shot, and we film a short promotional video during the session. Nothing rushed, nothing skipped.

One day of photography. Content you can use long after.

My objective is to give you more than beautiful photographs. I want you to leave with content that you can continue using to introduce your products, promote your collection and encourage people to shop.

  • One dedicated photography session.
  • Up to 20 professionally retouched photographs.
  • Photographs you can use on your website, social media, advertisements, packaging and promotional materials.
  • A video slideshow featuring your photographs.
  • A short promotional video filmed during our session.
  • Photographs delivered Monday afternoon, December 14.

Your photoshoot doesn't have to end when the camera stops

I'm also including seven additional pieces of content that you can use to keep promoting Turtle Threads Collection.

  1. 1 Introduce your collection A ready to post image announcing your collection to customers.
  2. 2 Show off your merchandise A promotional image featuring one of your products and encouraging people to shop.
  3. 3 Show your clothing in motion A designed video post that lets customers see how your clothing looks when worn.
  4. 4 Promote your collection on Instagram Stories A full screen design ready to share directly to your Instagram or Facebook Stories.
  5. 5 Give customers a reason to shop A promotional post you can use to announce a special offer, new arrival or upcoming release.
  6. 6 Share your signature message A beautifully designed post featuring your brand message, “Legacy Looks Good on You.”
  7. 7 Give your business page a fresh look A custom cover image for your Facebook business page that reflects the look and personality of Turtle Threads Collection.

These seven pieces are included in addition to your photographs and videos.

The goal is to give you more material to work with, so you don't have to start from scratch every time you want to promote your business.

Let's make the most of our day together

Before we finalize everything, I'd love to go over a few details with you so we can make sure the day is organized around what you need.

  • Will someone be available to help with styling and preparing the clothing?
  • Will the models arrive with their hair and makeup ready, or should we allow time and space for that?
  • Where do you see yourself using these photographs most?
  • Are there any particular products, poses or ideas you want us to prioritize?

The more we discuss beforehand, the better prepared we'll be to create something that truly represents your brand.
